artworks.title: Monumental aquamarine scavo corroso vase
artworks.summary: A large, heavy vase in aquamarine glass with a matt scavo surface, two applied ring handles and an undulating relief around the body. It carries a Seguso Arte Vetro factory label.
description: The rounded body rises into a tall cylindrical neck. Two ring handles of colourless glass are applied on either side of the neck, and a broad undulating relief runs all the way around the lower body. The vase is 32 cm high and 30 cm wide and weighs 7.5 kg, which is heavy for its size.

The surface is matt and finely granular throughout: a scavo finish, which imitates the weathered skin of glass recovered from the ground. The aquamarine colour varies from light turquoise to grey-green and a deeper green, with paler and darker patches. The foot is ground flat and is smoother than the rest of the surface. No engraved signature has been found.

A printed factory label on the lower body reads MURANO ITALY, SEGUSO, arte vetro, around a large stylised S. It is the main evidence for the maker, Seguso Arte Vetro, also known as Seguso AV. That firm should not be confused with Seguso Vetri d'Arte, a different Murano glassworks with its own history and archive.

Auction and reference sources connect Seguso Arte Vetro with the Murano glass artist Livio Seguso (born on Murano in 1930). Dealers have offered closely related vases in aquamarine and in white; the seller of the white example describes it as designed by Livio Seguso and made by Bisazza Vetro in 1993 (see Comparable examples). That makes a link with his designs plausible, but it does not show that he designed this vase. The model, designer and date of this example are still being researched.

marks.location: lower body, just above the foot
marks.observation: Printed factory label with white lettering on a transparent ground, so the glass shows through. MURANO and ITALY run upwards along the left edge; a large stylised S is followed by E / GU / SO, with 'arte vetro' below.
marks.transcriptionNote: Read from the photograph. The S of SEGUSO is the large initial; the remaining letters are stacked as E / GU / SO.
marks.interpretation: Factory label of Seguso Arte Vetro (Seguso AV), Murano. The period in which this label was used has not been established.

assertions.publicNote: Based on the printed Seguso Arte Vetro factory label on the lower body (see Marks & Labels). A label is strong evidence of the firm that made or sold a piece, but labels can be moved or added later, so it supports the attribution without proving it. No catalogue entry or model number has been found yet.
Based on the label, which reads MURANO ITALY.

evidence.locator: white example, dated 1993 by the seller

assertions.publicNote: A working date range, not a documented date. It rests on comparable pieces: a closely related white vase dated 1993 by its seller, and a Livio Seguso work by Seguso Arte Vetro catalogued as c. 1980. It will stay provisional until a catalogue or other document is found.

assertions.statement: Scavo surface, of the kind sold as scavo corroso
assertions.publicNote: The matt, granular and unevenly coloured skin shows the characteristics of scavo, the Murano finish that imitates excavated glass. 'Corroso' refers to a corroded or etched surface. How the surface of this particular piece was produced has not been established.

assertions.statement: Design associated with Livio Seguso: not confirmed

evidence.locator: Livio Seguso work by Seguso Arte Vetro
white example, attributed by the seller

assertions.publicNote: Seguso Arte Vetro is linked with Livio Seguso in auction records, and a dealer attributes a white vase of almost the same form and size to him. No document yet links this model to him, so his name is given as an association, not as the designer of this vase.

artworks.condition: Light surface marks are visible on the matt skin, including small dark specks and fine scratches. A full condition report has not yet been made.

comparables.title: Large Italian Scavo Corroso Aquamarine Glass Urn Vase
stated: No maker or designer named.
Blown glass with a scavo corroso surface, in a 'Classical Roman' style.
Height 30.5 cm, diameter 25.4 cm.
No label or signature mentioned.
comparables.comparison: Very close in colour and form: the same aquamarine tone, tall cylindrical neck, rounded body, two ring handles and undulating relief. The MURANIQ vase is larger (32 × 30 cm) and carries a Seguso Arte Vetro label. The two are probably the same basic design or closely related versions, but no catalogue or model number confirms it.

comparables.title: Seguso for Bisazza White Scavo Corroso Murano Glass Vase 1993 Signed
stated: Designed by Livio Seguso and made by Bisazza Vetro in 1993.
White to cream scavo corroso glass with two round handles.
Height 30.5 cm, diameter 30 cm.
Part of a Livio Seguso production collection made under Bisazza; the form is related to late-1980s taste influenced by Native American and Navajo pottery.
Listed as sold.
comparables.comparison: Almost the same height and diameter, with the same rounded body, cylindrical neck, applied ring handles, scavo finish and undulating relief, in white instead of aquamarine. It is the strongest indication of a link with Livio Seguso's designs. It is not known whether the two share a model number, or whether the Seguso Arte Vetro version was made before, during or after the Bisazza version.

Two applied ring handles and a continuous undulating relief around the lower body.

plausible: A design from the circle of Livio Seguso.
Made in the late 1980s or early 1990s.
The same basic design as the white vase sold as Bisazza, 1993.
A larger version of the aquamarine vase offered by a dealer.

artworks.title: Green scavo glass horse with gold leaf
artworks.summary: A hot-sculpted horse in light green glass with a white, weathered scavo surface and patches of gold leaf on the shoulders and hindquarters. It stands with one foreleg raised and wears an applied collar. No signature or label has been found.
description: The horse stands on three legs with one foreleg raised and bent at the knee. The neck is high and arched and the head is large and expressive, with an open mouth, flared nostrils and a pointed ear in colourless glass. A stylised crest mane in ribbed sections runs down the neck, an applied collar circles the base of the neck, and a twisted tail hangs down behind. The horse is 28 cm high, 25 cm wide from nose to tail and 12 cm deep, and weighs 2.15 kg.

The glass is a light, transparent green with darker green flecks. Its surface is covered with an uneven white, chalky crust that gathers in the ribs of the mane, around the collar and along the tail, while the legs are smoother and glossier: a scavo finish, which imitates the weathered skin of glass recovered from the ground. Patches of gold-coloured leaf, most likely gold leaf, are laid on both shoulders and both hindquarters. No signature, engraving or label has been found.

The model is very close to a brown horse with gold patches that is recorded in an auction-results database under the name 'Ferro Murano' and dated there c. 1940–1949, and comparable to a dark green scavo horse that an American auction house offered in 2009 as probably by Alfredo Barbini (see Comparable examples). Both are attributions made by others for their own sales. Neither has been confirmed by a factory catalogue, a signature or a label, so neither is given here as the maker.

'Ferro' does not point to a single glassworks: several Murano firms carried the name, among them S.A.I.A.R. Ferro Toso and Barovier Seguso & Ferro, the firm that became Seguso Vetri d'Arte in 1937. The maker, the factory and the date of this horse are still being researched.

assertions.publicNote: No signature or label has been found. Auction records give two horses of very similar form to 'Ferro Murano' and, with a qualification, to Alfredo Barbini (see Comparable examples). Neither attribution has been confirmed, so neither is given as the maker of this horse.

Based on technique and comparison only: the scavo surface and applied gold leaf are Murano practices, and every comparable horse found so far is catalogued as Murano glass. There is no label or mark to confirm it.

evidence.locator: brown example, dated c. 1940–1949 in the record

assertions.publicNote: A working range, not a documented date. The only dated comparable is the brown horse recorded as c. 1940–1949, and that date has not been checked against a catalogue. Corroded and scavo-type surfaces appear on Murano from the late 1930s and became widespread after the Second World War, and green scavo horses with gold leaf are still made today, so a later production of this model cannot be ruled out.

assertions.statement: Scavo surface with applied gold leaf
assertions.publicNote: The white, chalky and uneven crust over transparent green glass shows the characteristics of scavo. The gold appears to be gold leaf laid on the surface; it has not been tested.

assertions.statement: Ferro: attribution recorded for a brown example, not confirmed
assertions.publicNote: A brown horse of very similar form is listed in an auction-results database under 'Ferro Murano'. Several Murano firms carried the Ferro name, so the record does not identify a specific glassworks. The auction house, the full lot description and the reason for the attribution have not yet been traced.

assertions.statement: Alfredo Barbini: attribution suggested for a green example, not confirmed
assertions.publicNote: A dark green scavo horse of the same height was offered at auction in 2009 as probably by Alfredo Barbini. Barbini was a master of solid, hot-sculpted glass and showed sculptures with corroded surfaces at the 1948 Venice Biennale, but no catalogue, signed example or document has yet been found that links him to this model.

artworks.condition: The gold leaf is uneven and incomplete at its edges, and the white crust is rubbed in places; this may be part of the finish or later wear. A full condition report has not yet been made.

comparables.title: Murano Scavo Glass Horse
stated: Recorded under the name 'Ferro Murano'.
Glass, dark brown to amber, with transparent details and gold-coloured patches.
Sold at auction on 18 June 2017; the auction house is not shown in the part of the record consulted.
comparables.comparison: Compared on photographs of the record, the brown horse matches this one in every main feature: the long body, high arched neck, ribbed crest mane, applied collar, raised foreleg, gold on the shoulder and hindquarters, scavo surface and the shape of the head. The two appear to be colour variants of the same model. The comparison rests on photographs only; the full lot description has not been seen.

comparables.title: Early Scavo Murano Art Glass Horse
stated: Offered by Ripley Auctions, Indianapolis, on 31 May 2009 as lot 244.
An early Murano horse in dark green glass with a heavily weathered scavo surface.
Attributed, with a qualification, to Alfredo Barbini.
Height about 11 in (27.9 cm).
comparables.comparison: A green scavo horse of the same height as this one (28 cm), in a darker green. It supports the idea of one model made in several colours. The attribution to Barbini is the auction house's own and is cautiously worded; it is not backed by a signature or catalogue. The lot photographs have not yet been compared in detail.

comparables.title: Parade Pose Horse, green with details in 24kt gold leaf, scavo technique
stated: Artist: Pino Signoretto.
Green glass in the scavo technique, with details in 24-carat gold leaf.
Height 27 cm, length 29 cm, width 12 cm.
Listed as new and ready to ship; no date given.
comparables.comparison: Similar in size, pose and materials, but a different model: it has no collar, a flowing naturalistic mane instead of the ribbed crest, gold on the mane, tail and hooves instead of on the shoulders and hindquarters, and a fine frosted skin instead of a white crust. It shows that green scavo horses with gold leaf are still made on Murano today, so technique and colour alone cannot date or attribute this horse.

established: Hot-sculpted horse in transparent light green glass with a white, weathered scavo surface.
Gold-coloured leaf (not tested) on both shoulders and both hindquarters.
Applied collar, ribbed crest mane, colourless ear, one raised foreleg and a twisted tail.
Height 28 cm, width 25 cm (nose to tail), depth 12 cm, weight 2.15 kg.
No signature, engraving or label found.
Very close in form to a brown horse recorded under 'Ferro Murano' (sold 2017); comparable to a dark green horse offered in 2009.
Not the same model as the green scavo 'Parade Pose Horse' sold today under Pino Signoretto's name.
plausible: A colour variant of one Murano model that also exists in brown and dark green.
Made by one of the Murano firms named Ferro, as the record of the brown example suggests.
Made or designed by Alfredo Barbini, as suggested for the dark green example.
open: Which auction house sold the brown horse on 18 June 2017, with lot number, full description and provenance, and why it was given to 'Ferro Murano'.
Which Ferro firm, if any, made this model.
Whether the attribution to Alfredo Barbini can be confirmed or ruled out.
A factory catalogue, model number, or a signed or labelled example.
When the model was made, and whether it was produced over a long period.
Which other colours exist, for example colourless or blue.
